narrative:
The model estimates a 75% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your extensive overall experience of more than 11 years across all jobs was the strongest factor pushing the model toward predicting you would leave. Among employees the model expects to stay, only 15% have this level of total experience, suggesting the model sees long-tenured professionals as more likely to move on. Similarly, your 1–5 years in your current role was the second most influential factor, also increasing the likelihood of leaving. This tenure is actually the most common range among those predicted to stay, yet in your specific combination of factors it still contributed to the decision to expect departure.

The third most important element worked in the opposite direction: the fact that you have not received other job offers while at this company slightly reduced the predicted chance of leaving. However, this positive influence was not strong enough to outweigh the first two factors.

The organization should consider discussing your long-term career goals with you and exploring whether additional responsibilities, better recognition, or improved work conditions could increase your commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel more rewarding.
